podcast.body: An early disco hit that Nick Lowe greatly admired and intended to adapt into a power pop song, serving as the direct model for his track "Cruel to Be Kind." "Low modeled it after the early disco hit The Love I Lost by Harold Melvin and the Blue Notes."

podcast.body: Initially envisioned as a slow ballad by Gamble and Huff, this song was dynamically transformed by session drummer Earl Young. He significantly increased the tempo and introduced a "four-on-the-floor" beat with a prominent high-hat, an innovation that effectively created the foundational disco beat. "The session drummer Earl Young felt like it was dragging too much. So he sped things up with this four on the floor playing the bass drum on every beat and he hit that high hat symbol to drive the beaten holy shit."

podcast.body: This song was originally written as a ballad by Danny Gamble and Leon Huff. Session drummer Earl Young, working with MFSB, felt the song "lagged" and conceived the idea of "jazzing it up" by creating a driving groove with his kick drum and hi-hat, which became the pioneering "four on the floor" disco beat. "Danny Gamble and Leon Huff had written it as a ballad, but young thought the song kind of lagged."
